A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoSeg and LAVE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable, and renamed or relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original AutoSeg benchmark results, segmentation and captioning-cycle ablations, alternative-captioner experiments, and qualitative success and failure cases.

after.justification: v3 retains original segmentation experiments and adds component ablations, vocabulary statistics, mapper comparisons, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: BLIP-Cluster-Caption is renamed BBoost. The multi-resolution clustering, alignment, CRF and majority-filter denoising, caption generation, noun filtering, and segmentation through X-Decoder remain substantively unchanged. LAVE retains its mapping procedure and pseudocode.

E1.justification: The four quantitative benchmarks remain PASCAL VOC, PASCAL Context, ADE20K, and Cityscapes. v3 Figure 1 adds qualitative evaluation on Road Anomaly images containing a mascot and a road hole, providing a limited extension of test coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds LLaVA + LISA, while Table 4 removes OVSegmentor, SimSeg, OVDiff, and ZSSeg from the corresponding v2 Table 3 comparison. This substantially revises comparator membership. SAM + BLIP + X-Decoder and LLaVA + X-Decoder are retained from v2 Appendix B and promoted into the main comparison.

E3.justification: v3 introduces manually constructed per-dataset mappings as an additional evaluation condition in Table 4. New diagnostic protocols measure exact vocabulary overlap and average best-match CLIP similarity, and Table A6 specifies a one-cycle controlled component ablation. Existing benchmark splits, backbones, stated hyperparameters, and captioning-cycle sweep remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained segmentation and captioning-cycle ablations, v3 adds controlled denoising and caption-filtering tests in Table A6, vocabulary-coverage analysis in Table A5, and quantitative mapper validation in Table A7 and the manual-mapping comparison. These substantially expand evidence about component necessity and evaluation reliability. Qualitative failure cases are also revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained stochastic captioning and clustering cycles describe algorithm operations rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reported PC-459 baseline values change substantially between v2 Table 3 and v3 Table 4, including OpenSeg from 45.9 to 9.0 and X-Decoder from 65.1 to 16.1. AutoSeg's LAVE-mapped ADE20K and Cityscapes scores change from 5.9 and 29.5 to 6.0 and 30.0; VOC and Context remain 87.1 and 11.7. v3 also adds manual-mapping results, LISA results, vocabulary statistics, and diagnostic results. Manual-mapping scores represent a separate evaluation condition.

T1.justification: The encoder, clustering, alignment, voting, majority-filter formulations, and cmIoU definition retain their mathematical substance. v3 cleans up resolution indices, concatenation notation, and the presentation of normalized attention inputs. No new substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim automatic vocabulary generation and segmentation without additional training or user-supplied categories, introduce the BLIP enhancement component and LAVE, and claim strong AVS and competitive OVS performance. Renaming BCC to BBoost and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation of annotation ambiguity, vocabulary coverage, component necessity, and LAVE's agreement with manual mapping. It also revises failure explanations: the retained zebra-rug example changes from competition between parsed nouns to possible omission of 'rug', and a new vegetation-to-forest failure is attributed to overclustering. These extend and revise the scientific explanations beyond the retained benchmark discussion.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2's code-repository link and changes the abstract's availability statement to a future-release promise. It also omits the positional-encodings library disclosure, specific spaCy model identifier, and explicit LLaVA noun-list prompt. Main backbone and hyperparameter details remain. These are changes in documented reproducibility information, without establishing changes in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including LISA, the Road Anomaly source, a segmentation survey, and an NLP ambiguity review, and expands positioning around known versus automatically generated vocabularies. The main related-work categories and relationship to ZeroSeg remain consistent; publication-metadata updates do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial portions of related work and experimental discussion are rewritten. Caption filtering is folded into local captioning, LAVE becomes a standalone evaluation section, quantitative comparisons are reorganized, and the supplementary sections are reordered. Terminology changes throughout from BCC to BBoost, alongside affiliation and language edits.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, redraws the task, pipeline, and intermediate-feature diagrams, and expands and relocates the opening examples. Qualitative montages are reorganized with retained, added, and removed panels. Tables gain new columns, grouping, and highlighting; the alternative-captioner comparison moves into the main text, and Tables A5-A7 are added.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations and comparisons of LAVE with manual and embedding-based mappings strengthen evidence that v2 largely lacked. The improvement is limited by reduced code-access information and unresolved reporting differences, including VOC's stated one-cycle result of 85.3 in v3 Table 2 versus 87.1 in Table A6. Overall, the added validation provides a useful but qualified quality gain.
